question: Do the remaining forbidden 3.101.043 Bluetooth offload, HFP-AG, controller-dump, and vendor-HCI candidates have exact-target identities and register contracts?
prototype_hypothesis: sub_C3B7598 applies offload properties to adapter state; sub_C3B0DB0 and sub_C3B0DE8 accept an adapter and six-byte peer address for HFP-AG connect/disconnect; sub_C229F28 performs a no-argument controller crash dump; sub_C19F104 registers a vendor HCI tty by integer id and byte option.
callsite_evidence: sub_C3B7598 reads persist.bluetooth.a2dp.offloading, persist.bluetooth.hfp.offloading, and persist.bluetooth.lea.offloading and writes normalized bytes to adapter-state offsets +0x12, +0x13, and +0x14.
sub_C3B0DB0 copies four plus two bytes from the peer-address pointer into command storage and submits HFP-AG command 0x9B; sub_C3B0DE8 has the identical ABI and submits inverse command 0x9C.

sub_C229F28 contains bt_drv_reg_op_crash_dump, BT controller BusFault_Handler, controller register names, controller RAM ranges, and BT crash dump complete; it reads controller fault state and dumps the controller memory without incoming arguments.

sub_C19F104 stores R0 as the tty id, stores low R1 as a byte option, initializes the HCI transport callback structure, formats /dev/ttyBT%d, registers the device, and reports failure with bthci_register.
control_flow_evidence: Offload property names and exact adapter field stores directly identify the adapter state-entry helper.
Consecutive command IDs 0x9B/0x9C, identical six-byte address copies, and inverse command dispatch establish the HFP-AG connect/disconnect pair.
The crash-dump and vendor-HCI strings are exact identities rather than cross-version similarity; their hardware and registration side effects justify retaining forbidden policy.
ownership_analysis: Adapter state, HFP command storage, controller fault registers, and vendor transport state are firmware-owned. Peer addresses are borrowed and copied synchronously. All five entries remain forbidden and rejected because their side effects and lifecycle are outside the supported SDK contract.
unsafe_assumptions: Exact function identity does not promote these internal entries for direct module use.
Controller crash-dump execution can alter controller/host state and is not part of normal validation.
Physical offload, HFP-AG, controller-fault, and vendor-HCI behavior on exact 3.101.043 remains unprobed.
recommended_probe: Observe stock offload-state initialization and one HFP-AG connect/disconnect pair, verify /dev/ttyBT registration through the supported boot path, and validate crash dump only from a controlled real controller fault without directly calling forbidden entries.

artifacts.role: exact vendor HCI tty registration implementation
